checks.actual_behavior: Item-content RQ-VAE assigns three global residual code tokens; no per-user or per-prefix conditioning is present.
checks.math_types: Hyperbolic ball points and unsquared distance are used for assignment, but the quantization loss is tangent-space Euclidean MSE; does not match manifest's squared-distance objective or float64/boundary specification.
checks.nontrivial_hyperbolic_effect: The operator is genuinely non-Euclidean at curvature -1, but no controlled metric-only result establishes an effect; implementation and manifest definitions differ.
checks.numerical_domain: Distance clamps Mobius-offset norm below 1; mapped points are bounded by tanh clamp. This avoids boundary infinities but differs from the specified epsilon and smooth tangent-radius policy; non-finite inputs are not explicitly rejected in exp_0/distance.
checks.same_capacity_control: Nominal RQ-VAE dimensions match; exact candidate-vs-factor-four-Euclidean control and graph control are not evidenced by this source tree.
checks.user_future_leakage: The inspected Stage2 fitter uses Stage1 item embeddings and training target IDs only for fitting. It exports SIDs for all embedding rows, including non-training IDs; this is not event-label leakage by itself, but the manifest's exact Stage1/frozen vocabulary provenance cannot be confirmed from this tree alone.
checks.frozen_model_protocol: Several frozen constants are present, but candidate-source identity and exact controls are unresolved. CPU eligibility is not established; this verdict grants no GPU approval.

recommendation: Do not start a CPU study under this manifest yet. First bind the exact candidate source to the supplied candidate_id/hash and reconcile the code with the frozen distance-squared loss, numerical-domain policy, and explicit metric-matched Euclidean control. Only then can a CPU study be considered; no GPU approval is implied.
